parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing restriction is documented: no trans-specific criminal offence, no facility or birth-sex rule, no border or screening friction, no police targeting or violence record. The resident-facing machinery (legal gender recognition since 2007, gender-identity anti-discrimination law since 2005, unanimous 2022 comprehensive bill, marriage/adoption reform) is a climate signal only, but it points to a strong, unanimous institutional acceptance of trans people. The residual male homosexual offences retained on the statute book are a secondary, dead-letter factor per the rubric. Open questions remain: prison placement is unresolved (not documented as birth-sex enforced), and border/entry practice is unrecorded — these are unanswered questions, not exposures, and they keep the rating below the 0.85 tier. Extrapolating from the rule-of-law governance character and the documented acceptance, this sits in the reduced-risk band near the upper end.
